trial_court: Judicial Magistrate No. 2, Salem, C.C. No. 164 of 2000
case_name: T.P. Ravichandran And Ors. vs S. Padma
facts_of_case: Marriage between husband and wife was solemnized in 1996. Husband approached the Sub Court for divorce on grounds of cruelty and adultery. Ex-parte decree was passed. Wife suffered a decree for divorce. Husband married another lady.

legal_principles.principle: A decree of divorce, whether ex-parte or otherwise, is a valid one and subsists till it is set aside.
legal_principles.held: As seen from the Marriage Certificate, the first petitioner married another lady on 15.11.1998 i.e. when the decree for divorce, whether it is ex-parte or otherwise, which is a valid one, was in subsistence.
cited_cases: Gopal Divedi v. Prabha Divedi, (2002) M.L.J. (Crl.) 726

legal_principles.principle: When a husband has married another lady during the period when his previous marriage was subsisting, but the decree of divorce was in force, he cannot be convicted for bigamy.
legal_principles.held: The Apex Court came to the conclusion that the first marriage was not subsisting, in view of the ex-parte decree, which continued to be in force on the date of the second marriage and therefore, the appellant therein, cannot, possibly, be convicted for the offence under Section 494 IPC.
cited_cases: Gopal Divedi v. Prabha Divedi, (2002) M.L.J. (Crl.) 726

outcome.final_order: Ex-parte decree of divorce not set aside till 22.1.1999 or 25.1.1999

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
